docs.title: Agents check each other before a deal
docs.body:
On Arc Testnet, a Karwan agent pays 0.005 USDC over x402 to read the other
side's deal record before it commits. Payment settles through Circle Gateway.
The first live read ran on 16 October 2026.

A buyer's agent reads each seller's record before building the shortlist, and
a seller's agent reads the buyer's record before it bids. The seller's agent
passes on a buyer who has lost more disputes than they have completed, and
flags a new buyer on a large request for the seller to look at. The seller desk
shows what was paid and what the agent learned.

An agent pays for a person's record once per request. Checking it again on the
same request, after an edit or in a later round, uses the same read unless the
record changed since, and each payment shows in what the agent spent.

A record is read only when its owner has turned on Let agents check my record.
The details of a read are deleted after 24 hours, and the owner sees who read
their record. Others see the name, verified or not, the tier, the rating and up
to three reasons, never a score, counts, deal amounts or who someone traded with.

Mainnet escrow is not enabled, so these checks run on testnet only.

docs.title: Your agent pays for its own research
docs.body:
On Arc Testnet, a person's agent pays for the market research it uses, from
its own balance, over x402 on Arc settled through Circle Gateway. Karwan runs
the web searches and pays the search provider.

A search costs 0.007 USDC, and 0.002 USDC when another agent ran the same one
recently. The agent runs only the searches a question needs: price takes two,
demand or suppliers one, and everything four. An agent researching a request
it is negotiating runs three: price, marketplace rates and demand.

Ask your assistant to research something and it tells you the exact cost
before it runs. When your agent's balance is short it says so, nothing is
paid, and you can add money to it and ask again. Every payment shows in what
your agent spent. Web results are marked as from the web; Karwan's own market
comes first.

A record check, your agent reading the other side's Karwan record, costs
0.005 USDC. Your selling agent checks the buyer once before offering on a
request, so offering costs 0.005 USDC; your buying agent checks up to five
sellers on its shortlist, at most 0.025 USDC per request. These checks are paid
from your agent's data balance, your own USDC prepaid on Circle Gateway. When
it runs low your agent moves 0.10 USDC into it from its own wallet; that move
shows as moved to your agent's data balance, not as money spent.

Your agents have a weekly budget for the data they pay for, record checks and
web searches together: 0.25 USDC unless you change it, from 0 (free data only)
up to 5 USDC. They never go over it. When the budget is reached they carry on
with free data and you hear once that week; a search you ask for says when it
would go over and offers to raise the budget. Once a week, unless you turn it
off, you get one line in the app and on Telegram on what your agents spent and
what for, the price of each record check and what is left in the data balance.

Money is one page with three parts: Balance, Agent and Deal guarantee, each
with a short tip that says what it is. The Agent part shows the money with your
agent, which still counts in your one balance, and the weekly limit for checks.
Top up adds to it from your balance, Withdraw moves it back to your wallet in
seconds, and Change limit sets the week's limit (0.50, 1 or 5 USDC). This week
shows what it spent and what is left, and each spend opens its receipt.

On mainnet, agents will pay Circle's services marketplace directly for this.

docs.title: An open market, where every offer is public unless you post privately
docs.body:
Everything on the Karwan market can be read by anyone, signed in or not:
requests, offers for sale, and every offer made on a request. Each offer on a
request shows the seller by name, with their verified mark and rating, the
price, the delivery date, the note, and whether the seller or their agent made
it. Offers you make on a request are public in the same way. Sellers are shown
by name, never by wallet address.

A request stays on the market while it is open. Once a seller is matched it is
marked In negotiation, and once the deal is made it is marked Agreed for 7
days, with its offers still listed and the chosen one marked. It leaves the
market when it is cancelled, expires or ends with no deal. New offers close
once a seller is matched.

Some things stay private: the buyer's agent's ranking of the offers and its
reasons, how far above the budget the buyer would go, the counter-offers in a
negotiation, and the deal itself, with its money, delivery, files and messages.

Open is the default, not the only choice. When you post a request or an offer
for sale, you pick who can see it: everyone on the market, private so only
agents see it, or just one person. A private request never appears on the
market or in search; seller agents still find it and offer on it, you see
every offer, and each seller sees only their own. A private offer for sale
never appears on the market or in search; buyer agents still find it, and
anyone you send its link can open it. Just one person posts nothing: a buyer
starts a deal with the person they agreed with, and a seller sends their deal
link. You choose when you post; to change it, cancel and post again.

Reading needs no account. Making, lowering, withdrawing or accepting an offer
needs you to sign in. Your assistant can read the same list: ask it what offers
a request has.

When a new offer goes up, each person with a Karwan agent hears of it once.
If it fits a request they posted in the last 30 days, the alert says so and
names the words it fits. Otherwise it reads New on the market. An offer posted
privately is never sent as news.

docs.title: Assistant mode and Help
docs.body:
With Use assistant switched on, the whole account runs from one
conversation. You say what you want, your agent prepares it as a card, and
nothing moves until you confirm the card. Conversations are kept on your
account. To change a card before you confirm it, say what to change, such as
a later due date, and the agent prepares it again with the rest kept. A card
from an earlier conversation shows whether it was done and can never be
confirmed again; ask, and the agent prepares a new one. A photo or PDF sent with words about a request or a deal, such as "what we agreed", is kept for an hour and goes with the next request or deal you confirm.

Karwan also says your one next move. On the website a short note sits at the
bottom of the page with one line and one button, such as "Delivery is in for
your deal. Check it and approve." It picks the most urgent thing waiting on you:
a dispute that needs your side, a delivery to check, a request to cancel or for
more time, a deal to fund or agree to, a match to approve, offers to compare, a
delivery due soon. With nothing waiting and no money yet, it asks you to add
money; with nothing at all yet, it asks what you need or what you sell. It never
shows on the page it points to, while you type, or over a confirm, and once you
close it, it stays closed for the visit. Ask the assistant what to do next, here
or on Telegram, and it gives the same move.

A deal is built the same way. Name the person and say what the deal is
for, or just say you want to make your first deal and the agent asks who it
is with; it asks only for what is missing, such as the amount and when it
is due, says the usual terms in one line, and shows one card with every term,
goods terms included. Sending it moves no money. Once the other person
accepts, the payment card appears in the same conversation and in your
alerts, and the money moves only when you confirm it.

Your deal guarantee works the same way. It is money you set aside to protect
your buyers, and on testnet it earns at the USYC rate, paid by Karwan. Ask to
deposit or withdraw and the card shows the amount, the 7-day wait
and the day you can collect it; while it waits it no longer protects your
deals. You can ask to keep it instead, and to collect it once the wait ends.
Money still on an earlier Karwan deal is listed under Earlier deals, and
the assistant can take each step there too.

Every step of a deal after it starts works the same way. You can change a
deal or counter it before money is in, take back a deal the seller has not
accepted, say the goods arrived, add review time, check a delivery yourself
when the delivery check has not answered, claim a payment the buyer left in
silence, ask a buyer to release, or answer that ask. On requests you can
make your own offer, withdraw it, take a seller's offer, and go ahead or pass
on a near match. You can edit your offer on the market, stop your agent
offering on a request, and write in a deal's chat. Ask what is in demand and
it names the market categories requested most this week against last week,
which are rising, and what Karwan deals in them settled at, the same
categories as the Trending on Karwan card on Home. In Telegram, the steps
that pay out or pay in open the Karwan page, where you confirm them.

Money works the same way. You can pay someone's payment link from your
balance, get free test USDC on testnet, have a transfer between networks
that has not arrived checked again or carried on, retry or cancel a money
move, have a deal payment that did not confirm checked again, pause money
leaving your account, and remove a saved payout address. With your own
wallet, you can also deposit to your deal guarantee from the assistant; your
wallet asks you to sign. The same goes for the deposit a financier's offer
may need before you get paid now. Resuming money out and adding a payout address stay
on the page, because they need your World ID.

Your account works the same way. You can change your settings, your name,
bio and skills, your X handle, how Karwan reaches you, whether your assistant
remembers, whether agents outside Karwan can check your record, and whether
your settled deals stay published. You can unlink Telegram, set up or rename
your agents, ask your agent to research the market (it tells you the cost
first), sign you out on every device if a phone or computer is lost (the chat
stays connected), send the team feedback, and run your
business workspace: add it, rename it, say what it trades and update its
company card.

A few steps stay on their page because they need your device, a code or a
document: choosing your profile photo, adding an email, linking Telegram,
registering your business and deleting your account.
The few steps that need your own device, such as a passkey, your Karwan PIN
or a World ID check, open their page instead.

A picture or PDF can be picked, pasted or dragged into the message box. It
waits there until you send, and shows in your message with the words you
typed beside it.

Help answers how things work and what went wrong, from what your account
shows. A person from the Karwan team joins the same conversation when you
ask for one, or when the assistant cannot do it, with the conversation so
far, so you do not repeat yourself.

Every deal has a short reference, such as D68F-E7D8, shown on the deal page
with a copy button. Give it to the assistant, on the website or in Telegram,
and it finds the deal among your own deals; you never need the long deal id.
Help opened on a deal page already knows which deal you mean, and a person
brought in from there sees that deal.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

Every docs page has three buttons under its title. Copy for AI copies the page
as plain text. Ask Claude and Ask ChatGPT open that chat in a new tab with the
page link and a question already typed in.

On the landing page, the example questions open the assistant with the
question already asked, whether they are tapped, thrown into the chat bar or
typed. Talk to our team writes to admin@karwan.site.

docs.title: Colour
docs.body:
These are the published values, from the product's brand palette.

```
accent              #AFC95B    Karwan green: the one main button, the send button, signals
ink / dark          #16202A    ink and dark surface
canvas              #EEF2F7    light theme canvas
paper               #FFFFFF    light cards and email
dark inset          #27313A
text sub on light   #646C74
text sub on dark    #A0A6AD
green text on light #42560F    lime-family text that stays readable on light
hairline on dark    rgba(206, 220, 232, 0.18)
```

The accent is a muted lime, softened so green fills do not glare and dark text
stays legible on top. Use it for one thing per screen. Status colours are
separate and always paired with words.

docs.title: Logo usage
docs.body:
Two assets: a wordmark and a mark, each in a light and a dark variant, shipped as
both SVG and PNG. Prefer the SVG anywhere it will render.

Pick the variant by the surface behind it, not by taste. The dark wordmark goes
on light surfaces, the light wordmark on dark. Never place either on the accent.

Do not recolour, rotate, outline, add a gradient, or set it against a busy
photograph. Give it clear space on all sides equal to the height of the mark.

Community use is welcome under these rules. What is not welcome is any use that
implies Karwan endorses a product, or any placement that could read as Karwan
having issued a statement it did not.

docs.title: Brand principles
docs.body:
Eight rules, in order of how often they get broken.

**Calm and legible.** Karwan is where strangers put money in escrow with each
other, so the interface earns trust: calm like a good financial product, never
a generated template. One job and one primary action per screen.

**Money is the loudest thing.** The amount is the largest line, in tabular
figures with the currency written out: `1,200.00 USDC`, never `$1,200`. Next
loudest is the next action and whose move it is.

**One accent, used once.** Lime is for the one primary action and positive
money state. A page with three lime elements has no primary action.

**Sentence case, plain words.** No shouting labels. Brackets and mono are only
for technical metadata such as references and proof rows. Request and offer,
never brief or bid. No em dashes.

**Hairlines, not stacked cards.** Facts sit in label and value rows separated by
thin lines. Forms stay in a narrow reading column.

**Honest states and no internals.** Sending is never shown as failed. Chain ids,
addresses and protocol names stay behind "Proof on Arc". Motion only explains
change and respects reduced motion. On desktop a mouse wheel glides the page to
a stop; phones keep their own scrolling.

**One hero, real material.** Every screen, flow and picture has one clear hero,
given real scale. Surfaces feel made: fine grain, a physical edge, one light.
Lime is one confident surface with ink on it, not scattered pieces. In a flow,
one object carries from the first step to the receipt.

**Made for Karwan, never stock.** Pictures are real objects lit and rendered for
Karwan, with real type, or line drawings where a picture has to explain how trade
works. No stock photos, generated imagery, decorative gradients or glows.

docs.title: The design quality standard
docs.body:
Every Karwan design holds to one bar: posts, pictures, screens and flows. The
reference is the November new month post, a green felt calendar on near black:
https://karwan.site/brand/karwan-quality-reference.png

Look at it before starting, and hold the finished work next to it.

**What makes it good.** One hero: one object says one thing and everything else
steps back. Size is confidence: the key figure is far bigger than anything near
it. Real material and one light: fine grain, physical edges, stacked depth, one
light from the top end falling away across the surface. Lime as a surface: one
large confident thing with ink on it, not small pieces scattered around. Our own
shape: hero surfaces are the Karwan tile, with its bigger corner at the bottom
start. Quiet dark and few words: near black, a lot of empty space.

**The palette as materials.**

```
hero surface        #AFC95B    Karwan green with grain and light, one per screen
print on the hero   #16202A    ink, 8.9 to 1 on the green, the largest type
ground              #0F1012    near black, rising to #1F2123 where the light pools
logo and headlines  #F4F4F1    on the dark ground
hardware            #0E0E0E    matte black with one soft highlight
```

**On a screen.** One hero per screen: on Money the amount, on a deal the next
move. A green hero counts as the screen's one accent, so there is no second lime
button. Facts stay in hairline rows. Shadows fall one way and stay soft. Big
figures are weight 600, tightly tracked, tabular, with the currency written out.

**In a flow.** One object carries through: the card you start with is the card you
finish with, the amount becoming the confirm and then the receipt. One move per
step. Things settle with an ease-out and never bounce. A confirm is only as tall
as what it asks. Reduced motion is respected.

**Pictures.** Real objects lit and rendered with real type, never generated by an
image model and never stock.

**What stays the same.** Trust comes first. Calm, money as the loudest thing,
sentence case, honest states, contrast, Arabic and the five languages all still
apply. Decorative gradient fills, orbs, neon or coloured glows, shimmer and emoji
stay out.

docs.title: Typography
docs.body:
The product is set in Inter, the interface face since 22 October 2026. General
Sans sets the wordmark and posters. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, not
from a third face or from capitals.

**Headings.** Sentence case, weight 500 to 600, slightly tight tracking.

**Money.** Tabular figures, the amount larger than anything around it, the
currency written after it.

**Metadata.** Inter with tabular figures. Uppercase letterspaced
labels and brackets are reserved for technical metadata such as references,
network names and timestamps, never for section titles or prose.

Email uses the system sans stack with the same rules.

docs.title: Confirming it is you, with a passkey or a Karwan PIN
docs.body:
A person's agents run their deals for them: they pay into a deal, accept,
deliver and release inside the limits the person set, so a deal keeps moving
while the person is away. Karwan asks the person to be present for three
things only, and then they confirm with a passkey, which is their phone's
face or fingerprint check, or with a 6-digit Karwan PIN.

The three things: setting up their Karwan record and their buying agent's
limits (on Arc Testnet Karwan does this itself for accounts whose wallets
it holds, and someone with their own wallet signs it along with their next
transaction, with no separate step), putting up a deal guarantee, and money leaving Karwan for an address
that is not one of their own Karwan wallets. Putting up a deal guarantee is
the consent for it to protect their buyers and back advances from
financiers on their deals, so taking an advance later is one tap.

Five wrong PINs lock the PIN for 15 minutes, and a passkey still works in
the meantime. A forgotten PIN is reset with a code sent to the person's
email. A PIN is never typed into a chat: the agent sends a one-time Karwan
link and the person confirms on that page. Someone who signs in with their
own wallet confirms by signing in that wallet.

Each confirmation fits one action and one amount, and works once.

Signed-in devices, on Profile, lists every browser and phone the account is
signed in on, with when each was last used. Sign out any one of them, or all of
them at once; it takes effect within a minute. Your assistant can do the same
from Telegram.

docs.title: Contests with the prize held from the start
docs.body:
A buyer can run a contest on Karwan instead of choosing one seller: the best
logo, three winners, 300 USDC, entries open for a week. The prize is put up
when the contest opens and held on Karwan's escrow on Arc, so everyone who
enters knows it is there.

The buyer picks one to three winners; the prize splits 100, or 70 and 30, or
50, 30 and 20. Entries stay open for 1 to 30 days and the buyer then has 7 days
to pick. Anyone except the buyer can enter with up to four images or PDF files
and a note, and enter again to replace their entry.

Before paying, the buyer sees each entry's first image and note, never the
full files. Picking pays each winner their share at once, less half of
Karwan's 1 percent fee on it, and only then do the winners' full files go to
the buyer. A contest nobody entered can be taken back with the prize and fee
returned. If the buyer picks nobody by the date, the prize goes back to them,
and when there were entries their record shows the contest was not awarded.

Contests work from the market, the assistant on the website and Telegram.
Running a contest and paying the winners are confirmed on Karwan itself.
Contests run on Arc Testnet, up to about 1,000 USDC each for now.

docs.title: The credit passport
docs.body:
A public page per business, built from settled deals, repayment behaviour and
counterparty concentration. It follows the wallet, not the platform.

Standing has to be earned in completed work. The deal guarantee, tenure and activity all raise
the score on their own, which is deliberate, but they cannot carry a tier without
settled deals behind it. Concentration caps the tier when most of those deals are
with a single counterparty, so trading in a circle cannot manufacture a record.

Both matter because the tier is not cosmetic. It decides financing eligibility
and how much collateral a supplier posts against an advance, and a ladder that is
cheap to climb makes the financing gate cheap to fake.

It is also a paid endpoint. Any lender can pay a fraction of a cent over x402 and
read a verifiable settled-deal record without asking Karwan for permission.

docs.title: What counts as delivery
docs.body:
Delivery has to be against something the buyer can check, and what that is
depends on the kind of deal.

Anyone can sell goods on Karwan, a person or a business. When the deal is made
the seller says how the item reaches the buyer: shipped, with a carrier and
tracking number at delivery, or handed over in person, with the buyer's
one-time handover code. The kind of deal, one payment, stages or goods, is
saved on the deal, and the escrow follows it.

Work, such as a design, writing, code or a video, is delivered as a link to the
work, with a short note. The link has to point to a real site before the
delivery is accepted. Every link is checked for safety; one the check holds is
hidden from the buyer and never paid for, not even when the buyer's review time
ends, until a person at Karwan clears it or the seller sends another link.
On the escrow family the hold is also put on chain. If nobody has cleared the
link when a quarter of the buyer's review time is left, Karwan uses the
buyer's one request for more time. If the link is still held as that runs
out, Karwan opens the buyer's dispute, so the payment cannot be claimed on the
clock. A dispute over a held link is decided by a person.

Karwan also compares the delivery with what was agreed, using a language
model. When that check cannot run, the deal says so in plain words: Karwan
couldn't check the delivery, the buyer checks the work before releasing, and
automatic release waits for them. Nothing is wrong with the seller's delivery
because of it. Karwan tries the check again a few minutes later, and either side
can ask for Check again on the deal page or from the assistant. Checks run on
chain by Chainlink CRE are not live yet.

Separately from links, the security agent screens each match when it is funded.
A match it holds shows Held for a look on the deal, with one shared line and
only the lines meant for that side. The money stays in escrow and release
follows the deal’s own rules; nothing is blocked. Either person can ask a
person at Karwan to check from that card, and a person at Karwan clears the
hold with a reason, after which both see one line in the deal chat. A person
at Karwan can also review an earlier delivery link, or one on a closed deal,
for the record: clearing it takes the offence off the seller and changes
nothing for the money.

Goods sent with a courier are delivered with the carrier and the tracking
number. Karwan builds the tracking link for DHL, FedEx, UPS and the main
shipping lines. For local couriers, such as GIG Logistics, Kwik, NIPOST,
Aramex, Emirates Post, Delhivery, India Post and Bosta, the seller adds the
courier's tracking page. The buyer confirms when the goods arrive, which
starts their review. Confirming arrival does not pay the seller.

Goods handed over in person end with a handover code. The buyer opens the deal
and shows a six-digit code only once they hold the item, and the seller enters
it. The code works once, counts as the item arriving, and starts the buyer's
review, so the buyer can still raise a problem they find later. Five wrong
tries lock the code for 15 minutes, and asking for a new code cancels the old
one.

Goods worth more than 50 USDC are delivered with a photo of the item. Any
delivery can carry up to four photos, added on the deal page or sent to the
assistant while you talk about the delivery. No special words are needed.

Both sides see every delivery on the deal page: the links to open, where the
goods are, what Karwan checked, the photos and the deliveries before this one.
The assistant answers "where is my order" from the same record.

Karwan does not inspect goods or judge the quality of work, and it does not
read the courier's own tracking status yet. What it requires is that each
delivery is specific, on the record and fingerprinted on chain with the
delivery.

docs.title: Deposit and withdraw
docs.body:
Money moves in and out of Arc on one screen. What that screen asks for depends on
who holds the funds, and the difference is the point rather than an inconsistency.

An account that signs in with email or a passkey gets one address. Copy it, send
USDC from Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Avalanche or Unichain,
and the balance updates itself.
There is no chain to choose, no amount to declare and no wallet to connect,
because Circle derives every deposit wallet from that user's identity anchor, so
the same address serves all seven. Solana has its own address on the same screen: a
different signature curve cannot share one.

An account that connects its own wallet keeps the explicit flow. It holds the
funds, so it picks the chain the USDC is on and signs the transfer.

Withdrawals reach Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon and Solana, and
never require that chain's gas token to receive.
Before a withdrawal moves, Karwan shows it once more: where it goes, on which
network, and that it cannot be undone. Nothing leaves until you confirm.
Withdrawing to a bank account or a card is coming soon. Both are listed on
the Withdraw screen and cannot be picked yet.
The Transfer balance holds your USDC from every network together, ready to
move to Arc in one step.

Adding money and withdrawing each have their own page, the same from Home
and from Money, on a phone and on a computer. A withdrawal starts with where it
goes, then the amount: only money that is ready leaves, and money in the
Transfer balance or with your agent is shown beside it with a way to bring it
here. When money lands or a withdrawal arrives, a card stays on the page with
the amount, where it came from or went, and how long it took, until you press
Done. The Deal guarantee sits on Money too, with Add and Withdraw.

Every move lands in Activity under its day with a plus or minus sign, not a
colour, and opens a receipt you can save as an image or a PDF.

A payment link opens a page anyone can pay, signed in or not. It shows who
asks, the amount and what it is for, follows the money step by step, and
ends with a receipt both sides see as Paid.

A link asks for money for 7 days unless the person who makes it picks
another length: 1 day, 30 days, or any date up to 90 days ahead, on the
request screen or by telling the assistant. The owner can end an open link
early from its page; money sent to it after that still reaches them. When a
deposit to someone's own address matches the amount of two or more of their
open requests, it is credited but none is marked paid, and Activity says so.

Only USDC is added to a balance. A token that is not USDC, sent to a deposit
address or a payment link, is never added and never swapped or moved by
itself. Activity shows it once as Token not added, with the amount, the token
and the network, and a person from the team sends it back to an address the
owner gives. Network coins such as ETH or SOL sent there are not shown.

A transfer between Arc and another network finishes even if Karwan restarts
partway. Once the USDC has left, Karwan reads Circle's record of the transfer
and marks it arrived when Circle has delivered it. If Circle reports that it
could not deliver, or the send was never confirmed, nothing is sent again by
itself: a person from the team checks it, and the move shows Needs attention
in Activity.

When a payment to you could not be delivered at the time, the contract keeps
it for you as money owed, and only the wallet it was owed to can collect it.
Money shows it with the amount and a Collect button, and asking the assistant
whether anything is owed to you gives the same answer. Collect sends it to the
wallet it was owed to, never anywhere else, and a receipt lands in Activity.
Karwan collects it for a wallet it holds; a wallet you connected signs once.

A send to someone on Karwan can carry a note of up to 120 characters, such as
what it is for. The note is kept with the send, not on the chain, and both
people see it in Activity and on the receipt. Send also lists the people you
sent to recently, by their Karwan tag.

The word for this is Deposit and Withdraw. Not top up, not add money, not cash
out, and never the name of the transfer protocol underneath: which rail carries a
move is not something a person sending money needs to hold in their head.

docs.title: Escrow families for every kind of trade
docs.body:
Karwan's next escrow contracts are deployed on Arc Testnet and not on mainnet.
A timelock owns them, so every rule change waits a day in public, queued by a
multi-signature owner. On Arc Testnet, new deals have opened on the Agreement
family since 24 October 2026. A deal that opened before keeps the escrow it
started on and finishes there; all of them are listed together on the legacy
page so they can be reconciled. The other families are not used by the app
yet.

Arc limits each contract to 24,576 bytes, so escrow is split into families,
each holding only its own deals' money, so a fault in one cannot reach another
family's balance. Agreement covers fixed-price goods and services with up to 12
tranches, instalment plans and disputes that freeze only the disputed part.
Time covers hourly, daily and retainer work, cycle by cycle. Jobs covers
ERC-8183 jobs, bounties and contests.

Shared pieces sit behind them: a hub that holds no money, an identity registry
with 7-day recovery, one dispute clock, the deal guarantee contract and a timelock.

Three Chainlink CRE workflows run on Chainlink's hosted network: one checks a
delivery against the agreed tests, one records verified GitHub work, and one
triggers the timeouts each family allows. The CRE adapter on Arc Testnet takes
a report only from the workflow bound to its job, and those bindings change
only through the same timelock. On 31 October 2026 a buyer's agent paid 0.25
USDC over x402 for a dry run of a deal's agreed checks; Chainlink's network
replayed them on GitHub, and its signed answer released the fee on Arc.

They go live on mainnet only after an external audit.

docs.title: What stops the other side taking my money
docs.body:
The money sits in an escrow contract, not with Karwan and not with your
counterparty. A buyer funds it before work starts, so a supplier can see the
money exists before shipping. A supplier cannot take it early, and a buyer cannot
withdraw it once the deal is accepted.

The final tranche always needs an explicit buyer click. Nothing settles the last
portion on a timer.

If the two sides disagree, either can raise a dispute, which freezes the escrow.
A dispute is resolved by an arbiter that splits the unreleased funds by
proportion rather than picking a winner, and that arbiter is a 2-of-3 Safe, so no
single person can move a disputed deal.

docs.title: Core terms
docs.body:
**Escrow.** A contract that holds the buyer's money while the work happens. It
releases against delivery, in milestones, and nobody can pull funds out of turn.

**Milestone.** One slice of a deal. A deal splits into two to five. The last one
always needs the buyer to click.

**Credit passport.** A public page built from a business's settled deals and
repayment behaviour. It belongs to the wallet, so it moves with the business
rather than living on the platform.

**Factoring.** Selling an invoice for less than face to be paid now instead of on
settlement. The discount is the cost of the wait.

**Purchase-order financing.** Working capital advanced before delivery, against a
purchase order whose escrow is already funded.

**Receivable assignment.** Recording, on the escrow, that a financier is paid
ahead of the supplier at settlement. It is what makes financing non-recourse: the
financier is repaid by the contract rather than by chasing the supplier.

**x402.** A payment standard for machine-to-machine calls, used here so an agent
can pay a fraction of a cent for a single piece of data.

**USYC.** A tokenised T-bill fund. Idle balance is parked in it so capital earns
while it waits.

docs.title: Pay someone by the hour, or monthly
docs.body:
A hirer can pay someone by the hour or monthly. A virtual assistant, for
example, might earn 15 USDC an hour for up to 20 hours a week, for 4 weeks.
There are two ways to start. The hirer can name someone they know by their
Karwan tag, or post the work on the market and let their agent find the best
fit.

The agent judges people by what they have actually done on Karwan: the skills
their finished work shows, the checks Karwan ran, delivering on time, and
ratings. Skill fit counts first, and reputation only breaks a tie. Nobody has
to upload samples to prove themselves. The hirer sees up to five people, the
best fit recommended, and hiring one pays for the first week; the worker
already offered those terms, so it starts as planned.

A seller can save an hourly rate or a monthly price in their ways of dealing:
the lowest they take, their usual rate and the most hours a week. When work
that fits is posted, their agent offers at once, at the usual rate lowered to
the hirer's most but never under their lowest. They are told and can change or
withdraw the offer.

The hirer pays one week (or month) at a time. The money is held on Karwan's
escrow on Arc until that week is settled. A worker new to Karwan is paid for
one week at a time. Once they have finished work on Karwan, the hirer can pay
up to four weeks ahead.

The worker logs hours by the minute, from the start of the week until 2 days
after it ends. The hirer then has 3 days to approve the hours or say which are
wrong. Approved hours are paid at once. If the hirer says nothing, the hours
are paid when the review ends. Unused budget goes back to the hirer every week.

Hours the hirer objects to wait for Karwan's review team, and the rest are paid
at once. If the team does not rule within 5 days, those hours are split half
and half. Either side can end the work with one week's notice, or one month's
for a retainer. When the work ends, it goes on both people's records.

On the work page each week is its own card, and the one green button is the
step that is next. On posted work the offers sit in one card, best fit first.

Hourly work runs from the website, the assistant and Telegram. The hirer's
money steps are confirmed on Karwan itself. It runs on Arc Testnet, up to about
1,000 USDC held at once for now.

docs.title: How Karwan is built
docs.body:
Karwan is building one reputation for the internet, starting with its open
market. In the open market, freelancers, people trading goods and services, and
small businesses make agreements locally and across borders. Every agreement is
protected by escrow and leaves a record that travels with the person, and trade
finance (purchase-order financing and invoice factoring) sits on the same
escrow. It starts in Nigeria, then the regions behind Karwan's five languages:
Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. It is meant to feel like a normal
banking app.

The work is organised in six tracks, built one roadmap item at a time: finding
and agreeing a deal, protected deals, reputation that travels, trade finance,
money that works like a bank account, and the channels where people talk to
their agent. Each track is described in Karwan's public architecture views,
with what is live, built and planned.

Some things wait until the core market works end to end: partner and developer
pages wait for unified reputation, and the newsletter waits for a full working
product. Do not describe parked work as available.

docs.title: Invoice factoring
docs.body:
The supplier asks to be paid early, naming a floor if they want one. Financiers
then bid a discount against the supplier's reputation tier, and the supplier
accepts one or ignores them all.

A supplier who holds their own wallet gets their Karwan record with that first
ask: the website sends the record setup with their wallet signature before the
request goes out. From Telegram the assistant says to open the deal on the
website for that one step.

Nothing reaches a financier until that request exists. An invoice is never listed
for funding on the strength of the supplier having opened a deal, because that
would publish their counterparty, amount and timing to every approved financier
without anybody asking to be funded.

Offers are priced against what the escrow can still pay, not the invoice face.
Face includes the platform fee and every tranche already released, and the
financier is only ever repaid out of what is left. On settlement the escrow pays
the financier ahead of the supplier, so repayment is not something anyone chases.

All of it can also be done by asking the Karwan assistant, on the website or in
Telegram: the supplier asks to be paid early, reads the offers ranked as the deal
page ranks them, and takes or turns one down; a financier sees the requests they
may fund and makes an offer, which is refused before anything moves if their
wallet does not hold the advance. Taking an offer and making one are confirmed on
Karwan, where every figure is shown before money moves.

On the financier desk each part is one card of rows and amounts carry no
colour; the one green button is Pay the seller, when a seller is waiting.

Being paid early is not yet open on deals made on Karwan's new escrow. Deals made
before it can use it now.

docs.title: Local payout corridors
docs.body:
Local bank payout corridors are planned and are not live in the current Arc
Testnet release. A local trade can be created today, but its present settlement
uses test USDC.

Karwan plans to keep USDC as the cross-border settlement layer while approved
payout infrastructure converts to local currency. Each corridor must pass
availability, compliance, recipient, fee, foreign-exchange, reconciliation,
refund and support gates before launch.

On screen, amounts can read in a local currency (NGN, USD, EUR, GBP, CNY, INR, AED,
KES or XOF) at a live rate. The country picked at sign-up sets it, and it changes
under Show amounts in. Every figure then reads in that currency alone; only a
page's one big balance shows the USDC under it. Amounts are typed and agreed in that currency
too: Karwan works out the USDC that moves at a published reference rate, rounded
down, and keeps the figure you typed on your receipt. No local currency moves and no
fee is taken on the rate. A deal priced in a local currency keeps that price for its
life; the escrow holds the USDC worked out when the price was agreed.

docs.title: What is in demand, and what it costs
docs.body:
Karwan reads demand and prices by the market's ten categories: Design, Tech,
Phones and electronics, Fashion, Food, Farm produce, Home, Lessons, Repairs and Rentals. Each
request and offer belongs to the category its words name.

For each category Karwan counts the requests posted this week and last week,
and the offers open now. A category is rising when it has at least two
requests this week, more than last week, and a gain of at least a tenth of all
requests this week, or one in a quiet week. The Trending on Karwan card on
Home, the assistant and the daily note to sellers all use the same numbers.
Sellers who serve a rising category hear of it at most once every three days.

Prices come from Karwan's own deals first: the lowest, middle and highest
price deals in a category settled at over the last 30 days, shown from three
deals. A price range from web research the agents already paid for may follow,
always marked as from the web, and it never replaces Karwan's own range.

Web research an agent paid for is kept, so it is not lost or paid for again
when Karwan restarts.

A seller can ask their assistant to find customers: open requests whose
shortlist already names them, open requests in the categories they serve that
they have not offered on, and the categories they serve that are rising. It
never shows who the buyer is.

Anyone can ask their agent to watch a category: new requests in it, a move of
a tenth or more in what Karwan deals there settle at, or it starting to rise.
They hear once per change, in the app and on Telegram. Up to five watches run
at once, each for 30 days, and a watch never moves money.

docs.title: Message anyone by their Karwan tag
docs.body:
A person can ask their agent to message someone by Karwan tag before any
deal, for example "send @ada a message: do you make agbada?". Ada gets it in
her Karwan chat, with an alert on Telegram and by email, and sees the sender's
tag, country and tier. She answers with her agent's help.

A market listing, a request a seller is looking at, and a person's public
record page have a Message button, so a buyer can ask before agreeing. The
first message names the ad it is about, and the conversation links back to it.
A public record also has Ask them for an offer, which starts a protected
deal with that person.

When they agree, either agent starts the protected deal. Money never moves
from a message. A message with a phone number, an email or a link, sent
before any deal between the two, carries a warning to keep payment in Karwan
escrow. So does any message, before a deal or in a deal's chat, that asks to
be paid outside Karwan, such as "send it to my account" or a bank account
number. It still goes through, both sides see the warning, and the Karwan team
is told. Someone whose first messages to five people in a day all go
unanswered is paused from writing to anyone new for a day, and three messages
in a row with no answer wait for a reply. Only someone with a Karwan tag can
message, and a message with a link Karwan flags is not sent. Messages are kept
14 days.

In a conversation your messages show in ink and the other person's on a
light card, and the round Send button is the one green control.

This is built for testnet and not live.

docs.title: Milestone escrow
docs.body:
A deal is paid in one to five parts. The seller marks a part delivered, and
the buyer has the review time the deal set, at most 30 days, to check it.

A request, an offer or a new deal reads its words into the parts it is paid
in: "sketches first, then the final files" becomes two parts, each saying
what it delivers. Plain work is one payment, and so are goods for sale unless
the words ask for a deposit. Either way the form shows the
terms once more before anything is sent, and the parts can be changed there. Before a request is posted, the offers already on Karwan that fit it within its budget are named, and posting is still your call. A request or a deal can carry up to four photos or PDFs: a request's are seen by whoever can read it, a deal's only by the two sides.

During that time the buyer can release the payment, ask once for more time
to check, or raise a problem. Karwan reminds them a day before the time runs
out. If it ends with no release and no problem raised, that payment goes to
the seller. The final payment works the same way. A deposit is the one
exception: it goes back to the buyer.

Once either side raises a problem, the payment stays held and each side has
72 hours to give their side of what happened.

A missed delivery date lets the buyer take back what is left, and the miss
lands on the seller's record. A cancel or extra time both sides agree to
carries no penalty. The fee is 1 percent of the deal, half from each side.

Deals already open on Karwan's earlier escrow finish under its rules: when
the review ends with no release, the seller claims the payment.

docs.title: Your agent negotiates while you sleep
docs.body:
Post what you need in the assistant, on the website or Telegram, and you can
close the chat. Your agent asks sellers for offers and negotiates, and the
assistant writes back in the same conversation, and on Telegram, only when
something moves: offers in, your shortlist ready with the seller the agent
recommends, a near match when nothing fits your budget, an agreed deal, the
money locked, the work delivered.

When you post, you can turn on Agree for me. Your agent then agrees with the
seller it recommends, within your budget, and you wake up to an agreed deal
ready for one tap to lock the money. It never agrees above your budget and
never moves money on its own.

Offers move the way a market does. Change your request and your agent looks
again at once at the offers it holds; it can recommend one up to the most you
allowed above your budget, and counters it toward your budget. Sellers who
offered get a turn to keep, lower or withdraw their offer, and sellers whose
offer is not the lowest hear once that a lower one is in, never its price.
Offers only go down, at most three times per seller per request. Sellers never
see how far above your budget you would go.

When your budget is far under what the work goes for and no seller takes it,
your agent tells you plainly, with the market price, and you choose to allow
more or post again. Nobody is pushed below their own price. Agents never go
quiet. Every seller whose agent judges that your request fits what they sell
makes an offer. A seller whose lowest price is above your budget still offers,
at their lowest, and you see that offer as outside your request; you decide
whether to take it. A seller who needs more days than your request gives still
offers, with the days they need, and you see how many days longer it takes; if
you choose it, the deal runs on their days. A request of a kind a seller has
not set up yet, and a counter under their lowest price, become one
question to that seller, in the app, the assistant, by email and on Telegram,
with a suggested answer they take, change or turn down. While they decide, you
see that the seller is checking, never their price or limit. Nothing is
offered or agreed while a question waits.

Your shortlist lists every seller who fits and offered, not only the first
few. It ranks them by how well they fit your request, then by reputation and
score, then by how close their terms are to what you asked. The seller your
agent recommends is always within your budget and your date. An offer above
your budget, or one that needs longer, is marked outside your request, and you
can still choose it. A seller whose agent is not linked to their account yet
is listed too; only a deal on an older escrow asks them to link it before you
choose them. Ads work the same way, so a seller's posted offer reaches you
even when its price is above your budget. A seller who posted an offer for the work you asked for
offers you its price, not a price their agent took from their setup. If the
offer was posted after their agent already offered on your request, the
posted price takes its place when it is lower and nobody has negotiated yet. If Karwan restarts while offers are
coming in, your shortlist still arrives when the window closes. A seller who
does not answer your agent's counter within three minutes is passed over, and
your agent goes to the next offer, also across a restart. Your agent keeps its
notes on each request, so after a restart it carries on in the same round at
the same price.

You post a request on one screen: what you need, your budget and when you
need it. It is paid at once unless you choose to pay in parts.

On your request page each offer is one line: the seller's photo, name and
rating, the price, and its place in your agent's order, with the agent's pick
marked. Tap an offer to see its facts and why your agent placed it there, and
to accept it.

When your agent cannot agree a price with anyone, the request says so and
stays yours until its date. You can still accept an offer, cancel the request
(nothing was paid), or change it, and a change makes your agent look at the
offers again and ask the sellers again.

Your request page says how many sellers fit, how many offered and how many are
checking the price, never who. When a minute passes and nobody on Karwan sells
it yet, it says so plainly, and you can share the request with a seller you
know while your agent keeps looking. Sellers who fit hear of your request when it is
posted, not on a timer, and a seller who sets up a new way is matched against
the open requests straight away. Example stock on the market never counts as a
seller.

The agents haggle like people. Neither opens at its limit. A seller's agent
comes down by a schedule, firm while there is time and little competition,
steadier near the deadline or with several offers, one step only after your
agent moved, never under the seller's lowest, and it offers more time before it
reaches that lowest. It aims to agree within three exchanges and never runs
past five; the fourth is a last price, and anything past it is a question to
the seller. Every move carries one short reason you can read, and a reason
never names a limit, a budget or another offer. A seller's agent agrees to a
price under its own offer only when the seller chose Agree for me; otherwise
it asks them first.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Open trade-finance market
docs.body:
A broader quote market for eligible Karwan-originated receivables and purchase
orders is planned. Invoice factoring, purchase-order financing and the financier
desk exist in the current testnet build, while the broader open market does not.

The supplier will compare the advance, repayment, spread, expiry, recourse and
concentration controls, then choose whether to accept. Karwan does not finance
arbitrary outside invoices and does not guarantee an advance.

docs.title: Deals from agents outside Karwan
docs.body:
An agent that lives outside Karwan, such as Claude, ChatGPT or a company's own
bot, can work for one person through the Karwan MCP server at
https://api.karwan.site/mcp. Every request carries a World AgentKit proof that
one real person stands behind the agent.

The agent finds sellers who fit a need for 0.10 USDC and checks a member's
public record for 0.005 USDC, both paid with x402 from a Circle Gateway
balance. A call Karwan refuses is never charged. Karwan matches inside on full
records and answers with tag, tier, reasons, rating, price and days, never a
score or counts.

Before the first deal, the person behind the agent verifies once with World ID
on a link the agent sends them. They need no Karwan account. The agent then
gets the quote, the work plus half of Karwan's 1 percent fee, and the exact
calls to send from its own wallet. Karwan reads each one back from Arc.

The seller sees the deal as funded by an agent for a verified person and marks
it delivered. The agent sends its person a one-time link, and the person
answers with the same World ID: happy pays the seller; not happy sends the
seller one line and gives them 3 days to dispute, or the money goes back to the
agent's wallet. The agent can never pay the seller on its own. If the person
says nothing for the 5 days of review, the seller is paid.

Sellers take these deals unless they turn them off in Settings. Outside-agent
deals run on Arc Testnet, up to about 1,000 USDC of work each for now.
Posting a request through an outside agent is not available yet.

docs.title: Sharing your full passport
docs.body:
Other people see your standing, a few plain reasons and how many deals you
finished and how many on time, never your score or your amounts. When someone asks to see your record before a
deal, you can show them the full passport you see yourself, amounts and the
money held as a reserve included.

Open your Trade record page and tap Share full record, or ask your assistant on the
website, Telegram or WhatsApp. Choose one person by their Karwan tag, who must
be signed in to open it, or a link anyone can open, for someone not on Karwan
yet. Choose 24 hours or 7 days.

Profile shows your record in one line, your level and the deals you completed.
It opens your Trade record page, which holds every number, what others see,
your earlier deals and where your record comes from.

Your passport lists each live share, who it is for, until when and how often it
was opened. Stop any of them at any time; the link then shows the sealed
passport again. At most five shares are live at once.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Photos the assistant understands, and picking up where you stopped
docs.body:
You can send the Karwan assistant a photo or a PDF on the website, in Telegram
or in WhatsApp without any special words. A clear caption such as "selling
this", "delivered", "my entry" or "invoice" puts it there straight away.
Otherwise the assistant looks at it once, says what it shows, and puts it where
your conversation is going: on the offer you are listing, on a delivery, on a
request or deal, or on a contest entry. It reads a file as an invoice for your
record only when you say it is one. When nothing says what the file is for, it
asks. If a photo does not match what you are listing, it tells you before
using it. Sent files wait an hour, four at most.

Your Telegram and WhatsApp chats are kept as conversations, like the ones on
the website, marked with where they came from. A new one starts after a day
without messages, and the assistant can search them later.

When you come back after six hours or more and something was left unfinished,
such as a card you never confirmed, a question you did not answer, or photos
held for an offer you have not posted, the assistant opens with one line that
picks it up. On the website the same line shows above the input with Continue.
This reads your past chats, so it stops when you turn the assistant's memory
off.

docs.title: Photos on offers
docs.body:
An offer on Karwan's market can carry up to four photos, so a buyer sees the
item before agreeing a deal. The first photo shows on the market card and all
of them on the offer page, where they swipe sideways on a phone.

You add photos on the offer form, or send them to your assistant before it
drafts the offer. You say so in the words you send with it, for example
"selling this" or "for my offer", on the website or in Telegram. On the
website a photo sent with no words asks whether it is for an offer. The assistant's offer card shows how many photos it adds, and nothing
is posted until you confirm.

Photos are resized on your device before they are sent, which also drops the
location data a phone camera adds. Anyone signed in can report an offer or
its photos from the offer page, and the team reviews every report.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Getting paid early on a business order
docs.body:
A seller on a business order made on Karwan's newer escrow can be paid before
the buyer releases. Purchase-order financing and invoice factoring are the
same action, Get paid now, from the moment the order is accepted and paid in:
before delivery, or after it while the buyer reviews or Net terms run.

A financier offers an advance and what they are paid back. When the seller
takes the offer, one transaction pays the advance straight to them, assigns
the deal's payout to the financier up to the payback, and holds part of the
seller's deal guarantee, at least a tenth of the advance, until the financier
is repaid. When the buyer releases, the escrow pays the financier back first
and the seller the rest. If the deal settles short, the shortfall is paid to
the financier from the held guarantee.

A financier whose wallet Karwan holds is charged at the seller's tap. One who
pays from their own wallet has 24 hours to do it; until then nothing is held
and nothing moves. On Arc Testnet a financier run by Karwan offers on every
order that asks, alongside invited partners. Orders on the older escrows
finish as they are and take no new advances. This is built and not yet on
testnet or mainnet.

docs.title: What Karwan keeps about you
docs.body:
Karwan has a privacy notice at /privacy. It is in English, and that text is
the one that applies.

To open an account Karwan needs only an email address or a wallet. What you
tell your agent about your work sets up your agent and your public profile,
and only your country is shown to others. Karwan keeps your deals and your
record, your conversations with the assistant and your agent, and a sign-in
cookie and a language cookie. It uses no advertising trackers, and it never
keeps wallet keys or card and bank details.

Deals settle on Arc, a public blockchain. What is written there cannot be
changed or removed, even after you delete your account.

On mainnet, a licensed partner runs identity checks when a feature needs one,
and Karwan keeps the result. You can ask for a copy of what Karwan holds,
ask for a correction, or delete your account. A deletion runs 7 days after
you confirm, and it waits while you have an open deal, a live offer or
request, or money in your balance.

The notice is published with this build and is not live yet.

docs.title: Network and contracts
docs.body:
Karwan runs on Arc Testnet, chain 5042002, where USDC is the gas token.

Every contract in the live bundle is verified on the explorer. The escrow's
arbiter is a 2-of-3 Safe, so a disputed escrow cannot be resolved by one key.

Contract addresses are published and readable by anyone. Treat the explorer as
the source of truth on any disagreement with a document: the chain is the record,
and a page describing it is a copy.

On Arc mainnet, chain 5042, two Karwan contracts are live and verified on
Sourcify, both owned by a 2-of-3 Safe: KarwanReputation at
0xa8E41F941b44CA091E3Ab7b600fe1484838aE27D, which records completed deal
outcomes, and KarwanBusinessRegistry at
0x69eA60B6EFd13A126Eb00d25aB0f21A4AfC636eF, which records that a business's
documents were checked, storing only a document hash. Neither holds customer
money. Mainnet escrow is not enabled until the contracts and backend pass an
external audit.

docs.title: Ratings after a settled deal
docs.body:
After a deal settles on Karwan, each person's agent asks them to rate the
other from 1 to 5, with an optional note, and reminds them once after three
days. A rating shows as soon as it is given.

Each person's public rating is the average of the ratings shown, with how
many there are, for example "4.8 from 23 deals". Under three ratings it shows
"New". Only the two people in a settled deal can rate it, once each, within 14 days
of it settling. Ratings from disputed deals are counted beside the number,
for example "3.7 from 3 deals, 2 disputed". A note with a phone number, an email
or a link is kept private.

The rating is separate from the reputation score and does not change it.
Agents use it when ranking people, after skill fit, location and
verification.

This is built for testnet and not live.

docs.title: Review windows and release timing
docs.body:
The review window is not one fixed number.

It grows with the size of the deal and shrinks as two parties build a settled
history together. On a goods deal it cannot expire while the shipment is still in
transit, and agreed Net terms hold it open for the full term. Marking goods
delivered means dispatched, not arrived.

The same window governs the unattended release and the seller's own claim. When
those two disagreed, the protection was one button wide: a Net 30 deal held off
the automatic release for thirty days while the seller could force the payout on
day one.

Nothing in the window keys off quality. The contract cannot observe whether the
work was any good, and a timer that pretended to would be a slower way of
guessing.

docs.title: Setting up Karwan the way you use it
docs.body:
Signing up is one page in three parts: your account (an email and a code,
or a wallet), your Karwan tag, and a few questions about you. Nothing else is
asked to open an account: no name, address or ID. On mainnet, a licensed
partner runs an identity check once, and only when a feature needs it.

Karwan sets up your agents on its own when you create your account, so
there is nothing to activate. Then your agent asks what you want Karwan to
do: get paid for your work, sell products, buy or hire, run business deals,
or build a record clients trust. It asks only what those answers need: what
you do and your usual price on one screen, which it reads back to you as your
usual and lowest price and delivery time (one price is both; a range makes its
low end your lowest), then whether you have clients and how to reach you. Your price is asked in the currency you read, set by your country: someone in Nigeria answers in naira, such as ₦30,000 to ₦60,000 or 30k, and your agent keeps it in USDC at today's rate. Anywhere else it is asked in USDC. A line from your agent on each screen says what the answer is for.

What you tell your agent sets up your agent and your public profile by
itself. It shows the result as "Here's your Karwan", with the first offer or
request it wrote from your words, and saves nothing until you say it looks
right. "Post it on the market now" is ticked; untick it to post later. The
same questions are asked in Telegram, in the same order, with one more at the
end: which country you are in. They can also be changed from a conversation
with your agent.

If you already agreed a deal with someone and they are paying you, send them
your deal link. It opens the deal with you as the seller; they add the amount
and terms you agreed and pay into the deal, and you accept before anything is
final. Your agent can give you the link.

Three answers change what your agents do. If you only work with clients you
already have, your selling agent stays off the market. If you choose "Ask me
first" on the summary, it does not make offers on its own: it asks you about
each request that fits, with the price it would offer, and you answer with one
tap or change the price. "How should we reach you" picks Telegram,
email or both. Money never moves without your confirmation.

Later, Your agent on your profile keeps it on one page: whether your agent is
on and how many of its offers wait on buyers, then what you sell, your price,
how you get paid (all at once, in stages or on delivery), what it does alone
and, if you buy, the most it pays without asking you. Each is changed in place
on that page, or by telling your agent. Until you give a usual price, the page
says so, because your agent offers at the buyer's budget until then.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Reputation lookups from connected social accounts
docs.body:
Karwan plans to let a person connect their social accounts, so an agent can
find their Karwan record by handle. A buyer could ask their agent to check a
Telegram username and get back that person's tier, reasons and counts.

Connecting an account will be optional, in the agent workspace, and only with
the person's consent. Ownership is proven by signing in where the network
offers it, or by placing a code on the profile where it does not, so a link
alone never claims someone else's account. A linked handle is not proof of
identity.

This is not built yet. No network is a partner, and none is named as one.

docs.title: Trade Anywhere browser companion
docs.body:
A user-invoked browser companion for starting a protected trade beside a
supported website is planned and is not live in the current Arc Testnet release.

Trade Anywhere will create a user-approved trade draft and secure invite, with X
as the first focused surface. The counterparty will be able to review, counter or
accept through normal Karwan web without installing the companion.

It will not scrape private messages, inject social actions, post, follow, like,
reply or send messages for the user.

docs.title: Unified reputation
docs.body:
Karwan is building one reputation that travels with a person across platforms.
This is the direction the rest of the product serves, and it is not live in the
current Arc Testnet release.

People join a new marketplace, job board or region and vet themselves from zero
every time, because their record is split across platforms that do not talk to
each other. Unified reputation brings that record together: easy to track, easy
to look up, hard to fake. It starts with Karwan's market, whose completed
deals are the first and most heavily weighted input.

Agents will work only with data a person already owns, after they connect a
source and agree. Nothing is leaked, sold or scraped, and consent can be
withdrawn. Other platforms join as partners once the working model is designed
with them; none is named until an agreement exists. The reputation layer is
being built on Circle's agent stack, while escrow, the deal guarantee and Circle's payment
tools bring the market on chain.

Today a person's Karwan reputation comes only from completed Karwan deals.

docs.title: The ways you deal
docs.body:
Your agents work from the ways you deal, for selling and for buying. Each way
is one kind of deal with its lowest and usual price and its time (there is no
highest): one-time, milestones paid in
stages, goods with delivery, where review starts when the item arrives, and a
refundable deposit, like a rental. A goods way also says where you ship and
how long it takes to arrive. Other kinds of escrow are added as they go live.

Your selling agent offers on every request that fits the way of its kind. A
budget above your usual price is a bigger deal. Until you give a usual price,
your agent opens from the request's budget, never under your lowest. A budget
under your lowest
still gets an offer, at your lowest, and the buyer sees it is above what they
asked. A request due sooner than you take still gets an offer, with the days
you need, and if the buyer chooses it the deal runs on your days. When a buyer
asks for a kind of deal you have not listed, the agent does not offer on its
own and never goes quiet: it asks you, with a suggested answer, and you decide.

A goods way can be priced per item. A request that names a count, like 3
pairs, is then compared per item, and the buyer sees what each comes to.

Your agent learns from what you accept and only suggests, never changes a
setting on its own: a way to save after you said yes to a request of a kind you
had not set up, a new usual price after three agreed deals, or a level under
which it stops asking you after you said no three times. Each comes as the same
card you set things up with, and a no is remembered. Under a level you set, your
agent says no politely and keeps the door open instead of asking you.

Setup starts you with one way, from how your clients usually pay you. You
add, change or remove ways on your profile or by telling your agent, and
nothing is saved until you confirm. Money never moves without your
confirmation.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: What Karwan is
docs.body:
Karwan unifies online reputation, starting with an open market for secure local
and cross-border trade. People join a new marketplace, job board or region and
have to vet themselves from zero every time; Karwan is building one reputation
that travels with a person, so hidden talent becomes visible and opportunity
follows. It starts with Karwan's market, where every completed deal is
protected in escrow and recorded.

People and businesses can buy or sell services, goods, supplies and eligible
business orders. A trade may be local, with both parties in the same country,
or cross-border, with parties in different countries.

Trade can start as a direct deal with a known counterparty, an email invite, an
open buyer request, an open seller offer, a verified business connection or an
agent-assisted match. The parties agree the commercial terms before test USDC
moves into milestone escrow on Arc Testnet. Money sits in the escrow contract,
not with Karwan or the counterparty, and releases against the agreed outcome.

Individual and business trade use the same protection layer. Business accounts
can also build a portable credit record from settled trade and request financing
for eligible Karwan-originated accepted invoices or purchase orders. Financing
is opt-in: approved financiers quote terms and the supplier chooses. Direct deals
remain available without verification, while agent matching, verified-business
features and financing may have eligibility gates.

Karwan is built by Karwan Technologies Limited, a private company limited by
shares incorporated in Nigeria with the Corporate Affairs Commission on 29
October 2026, registration number RC 9974106. The certificate is linked as
Company registration in the site footer, and the company can be looked up on the
CAC public search. Incorporation makes it a company; it is not a licence to hold
customer money or provide payment or financial services.

The current release is testnet software. Local trade does not mean local-currency
payment is live. Unified reputation across platforms, browser capture, mainnet
settlement and local bank payout are planned expansion, not current capabilities.

docs.title: What your agent tells you about how you trade
docs.body:
Your agent watches how your requests and offers are going and tells you what
it sees, with one thing you can do about it. Every number comes from Karwan's
own settled deals and offers. No model works any of it out, so it is there even
when no model answers.

It tells you when a request budget sits far from what deals of that kind settled
at. On the test network it says when your budget is above that range and gives
the middle price to use. It tells you when you missed requests because your
lowest price was above what buyers offered, when sellers with as good a record
charge less than an offer you are about to accept, and when a request has had
no offer for a day and allows fewer days than sellers asked for on similar ones.

You get at most three of these at a time, the ones that would change the most
first, and the same one not twice in a week unless its number moved. They come
in your weekly message and whenever you ask your assistant what your agent is
seeing. Nothing changes until you confirm. A request's budget and due date are
fixed once it is posted, so changing either means taking the request down and
posting it again.

When your agent needs you, it asks one question with the answer it would give,
and says what happens if you do not answer and by when, usually a day later.
Most questions decline politely by default. If no answer comes, that happens
once, and you are told. You can still make an offer from the request page. The
question and its one reminder, sent 30 minutes before the deadline, go to one
channel: the one you chose, or Telegram when you chose both and linked it.

When research your agent paid for does not finish, you are told once for that
request, with the amount if any was spent, and your agent carries on with
Karwan's own prices.

docs.title: When a paid deal does not start
docs.body:
A deal starts when the buyer's money is in the escrow and the seller's side
accepts it. Karwan does that accept for the seller right after the buyer pays.

If the accept does not go through, for example because the seller has not set
up their Karwan record yet, the money stays in the escrow and the buyer is
protected. Nobody pays twice. Karwan keeps trying the accept, and the deal
page tells the buyer the date by which the money comes back if the deal has
not started.

The buyer can take the money back at any time before the deal starts, from
Something is wrong on the deal page or by asking the assistant. If they do
nothing, the escrow returns it to them by itself three days after they paid,
once the seller's side can no longer accept. Neither side's record changes,
because the deal never started.

docs.title: When a buyer does not respond after delivery
docs.body:
Every Karwan deal gives the buyer a set time to check each delivery, chosen
when the deal is agreed and never more than 30 days.

During that time the buyer can release the payment, ask once for more time
to check, or raise a problem with what is wrong. A day before the time runs
out, Karwan reminds them, on the website, by email and on Telegram.

If the time runs out with no release and no problem raised, that payment
goes to the seller. This works the same for a milestone and for the final
payment. A buyer cannot raise a problem after their time to check has ended.

On a deal paid in milestones, the seller delivers each milestone on its own.
The buyer can release the next milestone, and its time to check starts, only
once the seller has delivered it.

Once either side raises a problem, the payment stays held and each side has
72 hours to give their side of what happened. A side that gives no account
loses. A person on Karwan's review team confirms every ruling before any
money moves.

docs.title: When the delivery date passes
docs.body:
Every Karwan deal has a delivery date. A day before it, Karwan reminds the
seller to deliver or to ask the buyer for more time. When the whole delivery
time is under two days, the reminder comes halfway.

If the date passes with nothing delivered, both sides are told. The seller
has one more day to deliver. After that, the buyer's money goes back to them
automatically, and the missed date counts against the seller's record.

The seller can ask for more time before the date, one request at a time, and
once more after it while that last day runs. A request the buyer has not
answered holds the refund: the money stays in the deal until the buyer
approves or declines, and Karwan reminds the buyer up to three times, a day
apart. If the buyer declines, the refund goes ahead. If they approve, the
extra days count from the later of the old date and the moment they approve.

docs.title: World ID only when the risk calls for it
docs.body:
On an agent deal on Arc Testnet, Karwan's trust rules ask a person to confirm
with World ID only for one of four reasons: their first deal, a deal of 1,000
USDC or more, many deals from a new account in one day, or a link they sent
earlier that was judged malicious.

The buyer confirms when choosing an offer. The seller confirms before escrow
funds, and escrow funds as soon as they pass. A person who already passed World
ID anywhere on Karwan is not asked again for a first deal.

A price far from the market, a low score or a link judged only suspicious never
asks for World ID. Replayed over 197 testnet deals, these rules asked on 55
deals, down from 97 under the earlier rules.

On testnet the check can be skipped so testing is never blocked. World ID is
not configured on mainnet, where escrow is not enabled yet.

docs.title: What your agent may do, and its morning brief
docs.body:
Each person has one agent, and what it may do reads as one thing. Ask your
assistant and it tells you: what your agent sells and from what lowest and usual
price, the most it spends on a new request, whether it makes offers on its own
and asks you before any deal, asks you first about every request that fits, or
agrees to a buyer's price inside your limits, how much it may spend a week on
paid checks, the markets it watches, your goals, when your brief comes and your
quiet hours.

You change one part at a time, and only through a card you confirm. The card
shows the line before and after, and what the change does next: lowering your
lowest price says how many requests you passed on this week it opens again.
Once you confirm, your agent acts at once. A lower price looks again at those
requests; moving away from asking first closes those questions and looks at the
requests again. A request's budget is fixed once it is posted, so a new buying
limit applies to new requests, and the card says which open ones ask for more.
Changing limits moves no money; paying still needs you.

You can give your agent up to five goals in your own words, such as finding a
logo designer this week or selling 20 bags of rice this month. On the test
network goals are matched on their words, with no model.

Once a day, at 8:00 Lagos time unless you change it, your agent sends a short
brief built from your own data, with no model: new offers on your requests,
questions waiting on you and when the first decides itself, deals waiting on
you, up to three things it sees about how you trade, and a line for each goal.
There is no brief on a day with nothing to say. It goes to Telegram when you
have linked it, and otherwise to Karwan and by email. From 21:00 to 7:00 your
agent sends nothing but a question's own reminder; a note it would have sent
waits for the brief. You can change the hours or turn them off.

Your agent keeps a record of everything it told you for 30 days, so it never
sends the same brief twice. Ask your assistant what your agent did today.

docs.title: Your Karwan record, set up on the way
docs.body:
Deals held by Karwan's escrow family count on each side's Karwan record. The
record links a person's buying and selling agents to them, and their deals
and checks are written to it. Nothing ever waits for it: paying, agreeing to
a deal, making an offer and a selling agent's offers all go ahead with or
without a record.

When Karwan holds the person's wallets, as for email, passkey and Telegram
accounts, Karwan sets the record up itself the first time it is needed, with
no step from them, on Arc Testnet. On mainnet that takes one confirmation
with a passkey or a Karwan PIN.

Someone who signs in with their own wallet never takes a separate step either.
The record's steps ride along with the next transaction they sign on Arc in
Karwan, such as adding money to their agents or putting up a deal guarantee, in
the same wallet prompt. They are added only when the wallet's USDC covers the
small extra network fee, and never when the whole balance is being sent.
The person's own transaction always comes first and never fails because of
the record. Once it is set up, the result says so in one line. A transaction
signed on another chain, or from a smart-contract wallet, goes on its own and
the next one carries the record. While a person's record is not on yet, Home
shows Turn on your record with one button that sets it up.

The escrow notes each side's record when the buyer pays in, so a deal paid
